messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts observed across ingress (us-west-2). Error rate rising from 0.3% -> 6.8% in last 2m. Paging @sre-oncall-miguel and @ingest-helena. SLA impact possible.

sre-oncall-miguel: taking pager, joining. seeing upstream timeouts on batch-scheduler queues, headlock on big-model routes.

ingest-helena: confirmed. queue depth on the continuous-batcher service jumped from 120 -> 12,400 pending. many long-tail requests stuck at 'waiting for batch'.

runtime-ryan: looks like a kv-cache blowup combined with oversized batches. a few GPU pods reporting high mem pressure then restart loops.

product-liz: any customers already hitting 5xx? Support is getting DMs.

support-oliver: yes, three customers reported production failures in last 5m; one on Dedicated and two on Hosted via us-west. raising priority tickets.

sre-oncall-miguel: immediate mitigation steps: 1) throttle max_batch_size down to 8 on the influx routes, 2) enable small-batch fallback route, 3) scale up dedicated batcher pool by +4 pods. starting now.

ingest-helena: applying small-batch route flag (route: ingress-v2-smallbatch) to half of traffic for quick safety. patching config: `service.batch.max_size=8` on ingress-config.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered by ingest-helena: deploy/ingress-config v2026.03.15-rc2 -> success (3/3).

sre-oncall-miguel: also kicking eviction on oldest prefetched KV entries to free memory: `kvcachectl evict --age 30m --percent 20`

runtime-ryan: running KV eviction now. watching pod memory.

runtime-ryan: one GPU pod OOM'd and restarted during the spike, that caused backlog amplification. creating a mitigated routing rule to exclude that node.

ingest-helena: traffic split applied: 60% original, 40% small-batch. immediate drop in queue depth by ~40% reported in metrics.

support-oliver: customers' requests are retrying; one reported reduced latency after the split.

product-liz: any impact to persistent jobs or long-context sessions? risk of context loss?

runtime-ryan: long-context sessions on the restarted pods may lose ephemeral KV cache; recommend informing customers for potential transient reconnects. not widespread.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3317. Priority: P1. Affected region: us-west-2. Shortlink: https://redwood.prod/inc/INC-2026-3317

sre-oncall-miguel: I'll own the bridge. ingest-helena, runtime-ryan - please continue live debug. product-liz, support-oliver - coordinate customer comms & impacted accounts list.

support-oliver: compiling impacted list now: currently 12 developer orgs showing elevated errors, 2 have active alerts in their dashboards.

ingest-helena: additional telemetry: batching scheduler backlog correlates with a surge of long-sequence requests from a single API key (app-key-77). suspect heavy-prefetch test or misconfigured client.

sre-oncall-miguel: can we throttle that API key at the gateway? apply rate-limit 50 rps for app-key-77.

ingest-helena: rate limit applied at edge: `rate-limit add app-key-77 50` -> enforced.

ops-bot: Rate limit update successful.

sre-oncall-miguel: good. observe for 2 minutes.

runtime-ryan: after throttling app-key-77, batch queue depth dropped another 30%. GPU mem pressure subsiding; no further restarts. 5xx rate back down to ~0.9%.

product-liz: customer workarounds: suggest switching to smaller-model variant or reduce max_tokens; publishing note to affected customers via support tickets.

support-oliver: message drafts ready — will send targeted updates to the 12 impacted orgs.

incident-bot: Paging escalation required? If oncall needs assistance, react with :phone:.

sre-oncall-miguel: requesting runtime-ryan and ingest-helena stay for postmortem. will keep oncall active for next 45m.

runtime-ryan: plan for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = client-originated surge of very long sequences causing KV cache growth + oversized batching hitting mem and restarting pods -> head-of-line blocking -> timeouts.

ingest-helena: mitigation followups: 1) add per-key batching caps in gateway, 2) auto-fallback to small-batch policy when queue depth > 500, 3) tie eviction aggressiveness to mem pressure alerts.

sre-oncall-miguel: immediate follow-up actions (tracking): `TO DO: add per-key cap` assigned to ingest-helena, `TO DO: add autoswitch policy` assigned to runtime-ryan, `TO DO: customer-notes` assigned to support-oliver.

product-liz: checking if any SLAs will breach — finance/numbers TBD but will inform sales ops.

support-oliver: updating ticket statuses: two customers flagged as 'degraded' and offered status updates.

runtime-ryan: sanity check commands used during triage (for reference):
```
# check batcher queue depths
kubectl exec -it batcher-operator -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep batch_queue_depth"
# evict old kv entries
kvcachectl evict --age 30m --percent 20
# throttle API key
gatewayctl rate-limit add app-key-77 50
```

sre-oncall-miguel: will keep the bridge open until metrics stable for 30m and support confirms customer notifications. After that we'll transition to an async postmortem and RFC for per-key caps.

ingest-helena: metrics look stable at this time. queue depth ~450, 5xx ~0.7%.

support-oliver: customer responses: two orgs acknowledged the update and confirmed service restored. one asked for postmortem.

incident-bot: Reminder: please add incident tags and runbook link to INC-2026-3317.

sre-oncall-miguel: adding runbook ref and capturing logs. wrapping the live handoff: I'll mark the bridge as 'monitored' and hand off to the oncall rotation team in 30m unless regression.

product-liz: thanks all. postmortem owners: runtime-ryan (root cause), ingest-helena (mitigations), support-oliver (customer comms).

sre-oncall-miguel: closing live chat — shifting to async updates. ping me if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
